name: Localisation Rulebook
summary: Sites in more than one language or market: language, formats, currencies and switching.
check: Switch languages on a deep page: you stay on the same page.

rules.title: Correct lang on every page
rules.text: `<html lang>` matches the page language, and passages in another language have their own `lang`.

rules.title: hreflang for language versions
rules.text: Pages that exist in several languages link to each other with `hreflang`, including `x-default`.

rules.title: Locale formats
rules.text: Dates, numbers, currencies and units are formatted for the locale with `Intl` APIs, never assembled by hand.

rules.title: Room for longer text
rules.text: Layouts allow text that is 30–40 % longer than English and words that do not break (German, Czech).

rules.title: Language switcher in native names
rules.text: The language switcher lists "Čeština", "Deutsch", "English", in the same place on every page, and keeps the user on the same page.

rules.title: Translate everything
rules.text: Titles, meta descriptions, alt text, error messages, emails and legal pages are translated, not only the visible body.

rules.title: Local currency and prices
rules.text: Prices show in the visitor's currency where the business supports it, with taxes as local law expects.

rules.title: Flags for languages
rules.text: Flags stand for countries, not languages. Use language names.

rules.title: Automatic redirect by location
rules.text: Never force a language or country version based on IP alone. Suggest it and let people stay.

rules.title: Sentences built from fragments
rules.text: Never join translated pieces in code ("You have " + n + " items"); use full messages with placeholders and plural rules.
